claims.text: Encyclopaedia Britannica's account states: "U.S. and Israeli forces launch[ed] Operation Epic Fury" on 28 February 2026, conducting joint strikes on Iran "numbering nearly 900 in just the first 12 hours," and that "Khamenei was killed in the first wave of strikes on February 28, as were dozens of other top Iranian officials," with a strike near Bandar Abbas "killing about 170 people" at a girls' school. Over the following week, "U.S. forces hit about 140 targets with more than 300 strikes."

Encyclopaedia Britannica's running account reports that on 15 September 2026 the US military said it destroyed two small Iranian boats attempting to steal a US Navy sea drone; the conflict remains unresolved as the US House voted a third time on 15-16 September to end US involvement in the Iran war.

Encyclopaedia Britannica's news section for the 2026 Iran war lists, dated 18 September 2026: "Iran claims it struck an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, and other Mideast developments"; "Iran war's cost grows to $43.6 billion in new US military estimate"; and "Hundreds of thousands attend Iran's biggest government-organized rally since the war began." A 17 September 2026 entry states: "Senators from both parties voice criticism about Pentagon briefing on US defense strategy." No casualty figures accompany these items.

UNHCR's Operational Data Portal for the Middle East situation now records, for movements since 28 February 2026: 628,000 Iranian nationals who have crossed into neighbouring countries (22 September 2026, of whom 530,000 have since crossed back into Iran), 311,500 Lebanese refugees, all recorded in the Syrian Arab Republic (21 September 2026), and 341,228 new IDPs within Lebanon (17 September 2026, down from 352,793 on 10 August) -- a combined 1,280,728 people displaced or newly refugees across those two countries -- plus 946,000 Afghan (12 September 2026) and 1,038,900 Syrian (21 September 2026) returnee movements, a combined 1,984,900.

An Associated Press report carried on Encyclopaedia Britannica's news page (29 September 2026, 3:09 PM ET) states Iran's currency "fell to a new record low on Tuesday, with traders in Tehran exchanging more than 2.5 million rials to the U.S. dollar," a decline coming "just 27 days after the rial hit its previous record low of 2.2 million to the dollar on Sept. 2," attributing the collapse to the war's toll on the Iranian economy, international sanctions and a US naval blockade on Iranian oil exports.

Encyclopaedia Britannica's running news feed for the 2026 Iran war lists, dated 1 October 2026: "Third aircraft carrier and thousands of troops head to Mideast as Trump weighs new Iran strikes" (4:03 PM ET) and "Trump says Iran will be hit 'very hard' if it is behind copilot who tried to crash flight to Israel" (7:50 PM ET). Entries dated 30 September state Iran said it received a formal US response to its latest proposal to end the conflict, and that Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Iran's delegation to the UN General Assembly to leave New York ahead of schedule after negotiations stalled. No casualty figures accompany these items.

The same article reports Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes targeting U.S. embassies and military installations 'across the region, including in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Iraq, Oman, and Jordan,' and that 'commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz dropped more than 90 percent after the outbreak of conflict,' with oil prices surging 'from about $70 per barrel just before the war to an average of $103 per barrel in March.'

Encyclopaedia Britannica reports Israel resumed operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon with a ground invasion beginning 17 March 2026, and that this campaign had 'displac[ed] over 1.1 million people by late March.'

Encyclopaedia Britannica reports the memorandum of understanding 'was signed on June 17 by Trump and Iranian Pres. Masoud Pezeshkian,' setting 'a 60-day timeline for an agreement on the unresolved issue of Iran's nuclear program'; the article, last updated 21 August 2026, dates the conflict 'February 28, 2026 - present' and describes hostilities as resumed after Iran struck commercial vessels in July, with the deadline having since lapsed without a permanent settlement.

UNHCR's Operational Data Portal for the Middle East situation records, for movements since 28 February 2026: 568,800 Iranian nationals who have crossed into neighbouring countries (as of 13 August 2026), 245,600 Lebanese refugees (as of 17 August 2026), 352,793 new internally displaced people within Lebanon (as of 10 August 2026), and Afghan and Syrian returnee movements of 848,500 and 849,800 respectively (as of 15 and 17 August 2026).

Encyclopaedia Britannica's running account (checked 4 September 2026) states: "In late August, the U.S. military announced it had cleared all mines that Iran had placed in international shipping lanes of the Strait of Hormuz, reducing Tehran's ability to restrict movement through the waterway. Days later, U.S. forces attacked Larak Island, a small Iranian island in the strait that housed a military outpost used to monitor traffic, with American officials claiming Iranian forces were attempting to launch new mines from the location. The strikes prompted Iranian retaliation and sparked another round of military exchanges." It further states that, "according to U.S. officials in August," the U.S. military had established a passage "along the coast of Oman allowing the daily passage of 15-20 tankers and up to 10 million barrels of oil, nearly half of the prewar amount." No casualty figures for the Larak Island strikes or the ensuing exchanges are given.

UNHCR's Operational Data Portal for the Middle East situation records, for movements since 28 February 2026: 581,400 Iranian nationals who have crossed into neighbouring countries (as of 20 August 2026, up from 568,800 on 13 August), 245,600 Lebanese refugees (unchanged, as of 17 August 2026), 352,793 new internally displaced people within Lebanon (unchanged, as of 10 August 2026), 492,500 Iranians who have returned to Iran (19 August 2026), and Afghan returnees risen to 870,400 (22 August, up from 848,500).

UNHCR's Operational Data Portal for the Middle East situation, last updated 5 September 2026, records Lebanese refugees risen to 285,000 (from 245,600 on 17 August); combined Afghan and Syrian returnee movements of 1,879,600 (Afghanistan 922,600, 49.1%; Syria 957,000, 50.9%); Iranian nationals crossed into neighbouring countries unchanged at 581,400 (still dated 20 August), Lebanon new IDPs unchanged at 352,793 (still dated 10 August), and Iranian returnees unchanged at 492,500 (still dated 19 August).

UNHCR's Middle East situation data portal (component figures last updated 5-7 September 2026) records, since the war began: 595,100 Iranian nationals who have crossed into neighbouring countries (7 September, of whom 505,000 have since crossed back into Iran), 285,000 Lebanese refugees (5 September) and 352,793 new IDPs within Lebanon (10 August) -- a combined 1,232,893 people displaced or newly refugees across those two countries -- plus about 1.88 million Afghan and Syrian returnee movements (5 September).

description: A war between the United States and Israel against Iran and allied forces has continued since 28 February 2026, when nearly 900 US-Israeli strikes in 12 hours killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and dozens of officials, including a strike near Bandar Abbas that killed about 170 people at a girls' school. Iran retaliated across the Gulf states, Jordan and Oman, cutting Strait of Hormuz shipping over 90%, and hostilities have persisted, including a US strike on Iran's Larak Island outpost and, on 15 September, the destruction of two small Iranian boats near the Strait. UNHCR records 628,000 Iranian nationals and 311,500 Lebanese refugees displaced across borders since the war began, alongside almost 1.98 million Afghan and Syrian returnees. Diplomacy remains stalled: Iran said on 1 October it had received a formal US response to its latest ceasefire proposal, even as the US ordered a third carrier and more troops to the region and Trump threatened Iran would be hit 'very hard' if behind a copilot's attempt to crash a flight to Israel. Iran's currency hit a new record low on 29 September, above 2.5 million rials per dollar. The conflict remains unresolved.

impact.summary: The opening 28 February strikes killed Iran's Supreme Leader and dozens of officials, and a strike near Bandar Abbas killed about 170 people at a girls' school; no single verified cumulative death toll for the war exists. UNHCR's Middle East portal (updated 12-22 September) records, since the war began: 628,000 Iranian nationals who crossed into neighbouring countries (530,000 since returned), 311,500 Lebanese refugees now in Syria and 341,228 new IDPs in Lebanon -- a combined 1,280,728 displaced or newly refugees across those two countries -- plus almost 1.98 million Afghan and Syrian returnee movements. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz fell more than 90%. Iran's currency hit a new record low on 29 September, above 2.5 million rials per dollar, up from 2.2 million on 2 September, as sanctions and a naval oil blockade erode the economy. Diplomacy remains stalled: Iran said on 1 October it had received a formal US response to its ceasefire proposal, while the US ordered a third carrier and more troops to the region and weighed new strikes after Trump said Iran would be hit 'very hard' if behind a copilot's attempt to crash a flight to Israel.

location.region: Iran, Israel and Lebanon, with strikes and shipping disruption spreading across Jordan, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Iraq, Oman and the Strait of Hormuz

event.scale: Interstate war since 28 Feb 2026; unresolved into October, with a US military buildup (third carrier, added troops) amid threats of renewed strikes

name: Iran-Israel-US War

updates.text: The US ordered a third aircraft carrier and thousands of additional troops to the Middle East while weighing new strikes on Iran; Trump said Iran would be hit 'very hard' if it was behind a copilot's attempted crash of a flight bound for Israel. Iran said it had received a formal US response to its ceasefire proposal, and Rubio told Iran's UN delegation to leave New York early after talks stalled.

Iran's currency fell to a new record low on 29 September, with traders in Tehran exchanging more than 2.5 million rials to the dollar, per Encyclopaedia Britannica's news account (AP) -- down from a previous record of 2.2 million on 2 September -- as US sanctions and a naval blockade on Iranian oil exports continue to erode the economy.

UNHCR's Middle East portal now records 628,000 Iranian nationals who crossed into neighbouring countries (up from 595,100), 530,000 returned to Iran; Lebanese refugees in Syria rose to 311,500 while Lebanon's new IDPs eased to 341,228 (from 352,793); Afghan/Syrian returnees rose to about 1.98 million. Tracked Iran/Lebanon displacement total: 1,280,728.

Iran claimed it struck an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on 18 September; a new US military estimate put the war's total cost at $43.6 billion, and hundreds of thousands attended a government-organized rally in Iran, per Encyclopaedia Britannica's running account.

The US military said it destroyed two small Iranian boats on 15 September after they attempted to steal a US Navy sea drone near the Strait of Hormuz; the US House voted a third time on 15-16 September to end US involvement in the war.

UNHCR's Middle East portal now records 595,100 Iranian nationals who have crossed into neighbouring countries since the war began (up from 581,400), with the combined Iran/Lebanon displacement figure rising to 1,232,893.

UNHCR's Middle East dashboard shows Iranian cross-border movements rising to 581,400 (20 Aug, from 568,800) with 492,500 Iranians having returned to Iran (19 Aug); Afghan returnees rose to 870,400 (22 Aug). Lebanon refugee/IDP figures and the Strait of Hormuz corridor arrangement are unchanged.

UNHCR's Middle East dashboard shows Lebanese refugees risen to 285,000 (from 245,600) and combined Afghan/Syrian returnee movements risen to about 1.88 million (from about 1.72 million); the combined Iran/Lebanon displacement figure this record tracks rose to 1,219,193 accordingly. Iranian cross-border movements, Lebanon IDPs and Iranian returnee figures are unchanged.

In late August, after the US military said it had cleared all Iranian-laid mines from the Strait of Hormuz, US forces struck Iran's Larak Island outpost, which Iran retaliated against, sparking a fresh round of military exchanges; the US has since maintained an escorted corridor off Oman's coast carrying 15-20 tankers and up to 10 million barrels of oil daily, about half the prewar volume.
